voice.direction: Warm, confident male storyteller, brisk documentary pace (about 165 words per minute), curious on the opening question, punchy on every number, a wry smile on the twist. No music, no effects.

characters.name: Ray
characters.descriptor: an adult male stickman of average build: perfectly smooth glossy white ball head, no ears, no nose, no hair, face drawn in flat black lines; a dark chocolate-brown wool flat cap sitting on top of the ball head; a mustard-yellow knit cardigan with exactly 4 round brown buttons over a crisp white collared shirt; dark navy trousers; small brown leather shoes; white mitten hands with 4 fingers.

characters.name: the cashier
characters.descriptor: an adult female stickman, slim shoulders, no beard or stubble: perfectly smooth glossy white ball head, no ears, no nose, face drawn in flat black lines with small eyelashes; a short glossy dark-brown bob haircut sitting on the ball head; a simple green apron over a white short-sleeved shirt; black trousers; white mitten hands.

locations.descriptor: a small American corner grocery store seen from the customer side: on the LEFT a long checkout counter running from the foreground toward the back with a cash register at its front end and the cashier's spot behind it; in the CENTRE open floor where the customer stands; at the BACK wooden shelves full of colourful cans and boxes; on the RIGHT a large shop window showing the street and one parked car; black-and-white checkerboard floor; warm morning light from the window.

variants.changes: 1950s look: pastel mint-green walls, chrome-and-red counter, chrome vintage cash register, a pastel-green 1950s car outside.
today's look: bright white walls with LED strip lights, white modern counter, sleek tap-to-pay terminal instead of a cash register, a white electric car outside.

props.descriptor: a classic white sliced bread loaf in a clear plastic bag with a red twist tie
a closed grey pulp-paper egg carton holding one dozen eggs
a white plastic one-gallon milk jug with a red cap and a plain white label with no words
a brown paper grocery bag standing upright, full, with the sliced bread loaf, the grey egg carton and the white milk jug sticking out of the top
a single green US ten-dollar bill, simplified, with no readable text

scenes.line: How much breakfast could $10 buy over the last 80 years?
scenes.spoken: How much breakfast could ten dollars buy over the last eighty years?
scenes.moment: Ray slaps a single ten-dollar bill flat onto the counter with a proud grin; beside him on the counter stand the grocery bags; the cashier smiles behind the register.
scenes.camera: medium-wide, eye level, Ray in the centre third facing camera
scenes.motion: Ray lifts his hand and slaps the bill down on the counter, then turns to the camera with a proud grin; the cashier claps once.
scenes.camera_move: slow push-in, Ray keeps facing camera
scenes.sfx: paper slap, vintage register bell, soft store ambience

scenes.spoken: Nineteen fifty. The list costs about a dollar fifty-seven.
scenes.moment: Ray holds up a small paper shopping list; the bread loaf, the egg carton and the milk jug float beside him, softly glowing.

scenes.line: Today: $8.28. One bag, and $1.72 in change.
scenes.spoken: Today: eight dollars twenty-eight. One bag, and a dollar seventy-two in change.
scenes.moment: Ray holds one grocery bag in his left arm and stares at a single one-dollar bill and a few coins in his open right hand, unimpressed.
scenes.motion: Ray looks down at the change in his hand, sighs, then looks at the camera with a wry face.
scenes.camera_move: slow tilt down to the hand, then back up to his face

thumbnails.moment: close-up of Ray's shocked face on the right, holding a ten-dollar bill toward camera; on the left a towering stack of six grocery bags.
split screen: left half 1950 with Ray grinning beside six bags, right half today with Ray frowning holding one bag, a jagged red line between them.
Ray peering into a single nearly empty grocery bag with one egg inside, dramatic top light, dark background.
